llm_response.content:
Empirical Research Plan – “Traffic Congestion, Local Vehicle Emissions and Fetal Health”

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Strategy: Staggered Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event-study extension and mother fixed effects.

Why this is appropriate
• Policy variation is discrete (E-ZPass is switched on at each toll plaza on a known date).  
• Adoption dates differ across 98 plazas between 1997-2001 ⇒ classic staggered rollout.  
• Vital-statistics addresses let us map every birth to distance from each plaza, creating narrowly defined “exposed” and “non-exposed” groups.  
• Fetal health outcomes are observed for many periods before and after adoption, enabling pre-trend tests and dynamic effects.  
• Linkable maternal identifiers allow within-mother comparisons, dramatically strengthening causal claims by absorbing all time-invariant maternal traits.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control Definition
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment indicator  
Treat_i,t  = 1 if mother i’s residential address lies within 2 km of a toll plaza that has already adopted E-ZPass for at least the last two trimesters of the pregnancy whose birth occurs at time t.  
(Several sensitivity radii: 1 km, 3 km.)

Control group  
Primary: Mothers living 2–10 km from the same (or any) toll plaza whose pregnancy overlaps the same calendar time but who are sufficiently far that emissions from queuing cars are negligible. The 2 km inner ring vs 2–10 km outer ring is a “donut” that keeps both groups close enough to share broader labor-market and health-care environments.

Treatment timing  
Event date = plaza-specific E-ZPass go-live day. For each birth we compute the conception month (birth date – gestational age). A birth is coded “post” only if ≥ 180 gestational days occur after the event; births already in late pregnancy when the switch occurs are coded as “pre.” We will build an event-time variable k = {-6,…,6} measuring trimesters relative to adoption for the event-study.

Running variable and cutoff  
Not applicable (DiD, not RDD).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Trends. Absent E-ZPass, time-paths of fetal-health outcomes for mothers ≤ 2 km and 2–10 km from plazas would have moved in parallel.

Plausibility: Short distances mean exposed and control mothers face the same county health policies, hospitals, business cycles, weather, etc.; only high-frequency emissions differ. Will be tested with pre-event leads.

A2. No Anticipatory Behavior. Families do not time pregnancies or move in/out in anticipation of E-ZPass within the short (≈ 1-year) planning horizon.

Plausibility: Adoption dates were driven by highway-agency engineering schedules, unknown to most households.

A3. No Concurrent Confounding Interventions Within 10 km. Other contemporaneous highway or industrial changes are not systematically aligned with the switch dates.

Plausibility: We will include plaza-specific linear trends and county-by-year FEs; plus placebo checks at plazas that adopted later.

A4. Stable Composition (SUTVA / no spillovers). E-ZPass at one plaza does not materially change air quality for mothers > 2 km away.

Plausibility: Engineering evidence shows emissions fall sharply within 1.5–2 km; highway flow further away changes little. Will test using EPA monitors ≥ 4 km.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigation
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Threat 1: Residential sorting after E-ZPass because nearby housing prices rise.  
Mitigation:  
• Mother fixed effects: keep only mothers observed in multiple births who did NOT move (address constant within 50 m) between births.  
• Complement with housing-price DiD to document sorting magnitude; if large, re-estimate on first births only (unlikely to move because of pregnancy).

Threat 2: Differential pre-trends.  
Mitigation: Event-study plot of coefficients for k = -6,…,-1 must be statistically flat. If violated, re-specify with plaza-specific trends or restrict to shorter windows.

Threat 3: Pollution drift to control ring or region-wide traffic improvements (spillovers).  
Mitigation:  
• 2–10 km ring purposely small but outside plume line; repeat using mothers 10–20 km away as alt control.  
• Validate spatial decay using NO₂ monitor data in monitor-by-event DiD.  
• Triple-difference: near vs far * before vs after * high-traffic vs low-traffic time-of-day conception windows.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---------------- SET-UP ----------------
library(data.table)     # fast data wrangling
library(sf)             # spatial joins
library(fixest)         # high-dim FE regressions
library(lubridate)

# ---------------- LOAD DATA -------------
birth <- fread("pa_nj_births.csv")   # confidential vital stats
plaza <- fread("toll_plaza_dates.csv") # plaza_id, lat, lon, ezpass_date
poll  <- fread("epa_monitors.csv")   # optional robustness

# ---------------- GEO-MATCH -------------
birth_sf <- st_as_sf(birth, coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326)
plaza_sf <- st_as_sf(plaza, coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326)

# Compute distance to nearest plaza & id
nn <- st_nearest_feature(birth_sf, plaza_sf)
birth_sf$plaza_id  <- plaza$plaza_id[nn]
birth_sf$dist_km   <- st_distance(birth_sf, plaza_sf[nn, ], by_element = TRUE)/1000

# ---------------- TIME RELATIVE TO ADOPTION -------------
birth_sf$ez_date <- plaza$ezpass_date[match(birth_sf$plaza_id, plaza$plaza_id)]
birth_sf$birth_date <- as.Date(birth_sf$birth_date)
birth_sf$conception_date <- birth_sf$birth_date - weeks(birth_sf$gest_weeks)

# at least 180 gest days after adoption
birth_sf$post <- as.integer(birth_sf$conception_date >= (birth_sf$ez_date + 100))  # ~14 weeks

# Event time in trimesters
birth_sf$event_tri <- floor(as.numeric(difftime(birth_sf$conception_date, 
                                                birth_sf$ez_date, units="days"))/90)

# ---------------- TREATMENT DUMMY -------------
birth_sf$treated <- (birth_sf$dist_km <= 2)

# Keep sample within 10 km donut
sub <- birth_sf[birth_sf$dist_km<=10,]

# ---------------- MAIN SPEC ----------------
formula_main <- low_birth_weight ~ treated*post + 
                mom_age + parity + smoker + black + hispanic +
                i(year, treated, ref=1997) | 
                mom_id + plaza_id + year_month          # FEs

est <- feols(formula_main, data=sub, cluster = ~plaza_id)
summary(est)

# ---------------- EVENT STUDY --------------
sub$k <- pmax(pmin(sub$event_tri,6),-6)   # cap at ±6
event <- feols(low_birth_weight ~ i(k, treated, ref = -1) | mom_id + plaza_id + year_month,
               data=sub, cluster=~plaza_id)
iplot(event)

# ---------------- ROBUSTNESS: Alternate radius 1 km ------------
sub1 <- birth_sf[birth_sf$dist_km<=1 | birth_sf$dist_km>5 & birth_sf$dist_km<=10,]
sub1$treated1 <- (sub1$dist_km<=1)
est_r <- feols(low_birth_weight ~ treated1*post + 
                 controls | mom_id + plaza_id + year_month, data=sub1,
                 cluster=~plaza_id)
etable(est, est_r)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory and prior epidemiology suggest a negative effect of traffic-related pollutants on fetal health; therefore I expect:

• Low birth weight prevalence to drop 0.8–1.2 pp (≈ 10–15 %) among the treated.  
• Mean birth weight to rise ≈ 20–25 g.  
• Pre-term (< 38 weeks) incidence to fall ≈ 0.6 pp.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: No differential pre-trends ………………… 0.8  
C2: Treatment exogenous to outcome ………… 0.9  
C3: No interference / spillovers ……………… 0.6  
C4: Stable unit composition …………………… 0.7  
C5: Correct functional form / timing ……… 0.9  

(Scale: 1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = uncertain; values are my subjective scores.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
